_comment: One file for the three assistants; gui.mode picks one ("agent", "rag" or "rag_agentic"), also from the settings. llm: the endpoint every mode uses. salome, policy, work_dir: the SALOME Agent only. rag: the two documentation modes (rag.chatbot.agentic: the agentic one only). Keys starting with _ are comments.

rag._comment: Documentation modes (gui.mode "rag" or "rag_agentic"): raglib answers questions from the SALOME HTML documentation. 'chatbot' and 'extraction' each follow raglib's own config.json schema (raglib/README.md). Relative paths are resolved against this file's directory; ~, $VAR and ${VAR:-fallback} are expanded (SALOME's environment sets $DOCUMENTATION_ROOT_DIR and $<MODULE>_ROOT_DIR).

chatbot._comment_project_name: No spaces: names the ChromaDB collection. Must match extraction.project_name.
chatbot._comment_llm: No 'llm' block: the shared llm.base_url / model / api_key / ssl_cert_file above are used. Add {"llm": {"model": "..."}} here to override any of them for the documentation modes only.

embedding._comment: 'local' runs sentence-transformers here; 'api' uses an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint. Must stay identical to extraction.embedding.

chatbot._comment_agentic: Needed by the agentic RAG mode only. page_index.json is written by the index build (extraction.output_dir).

extraction._comment_modules: Documentation of the SALOME being used, found through its environment: $DOCUMENTATION_ROOT_DIR (the DOCUMENTATION module, which gathers every module's docs), else each module's own $<MODULE>_ROOT_DIR. Both are set by SALOME (env_launch.sh, salome shell) and kept by the plugin; outside SALOME export DOCUMENTATION_ROOT_DIR=<SALOME>/INSTALL/DOCUMENTATION. ${VAR:-fallback} is the shell's syntax; absolute and relative paths work too. dev_path = API reference (tui), user_path = user guide (gui); a path that does not exist is skipped. No _comment key inside modules itself.

GEOM.description: Geometry module: CAD construction and manipulation.

SMESH.description: Mesh module: meshing algorithms and mesh editing.
